**Danske Multidisciplinære Psykiatrigrupper (DMPGer)** is a professional partnership in Denmark that plays a central role in developing clinical guidelines for the assessment and treatment of ADHD across both adult and child/youth sectors, in both hospital and private settings [^src1]. The organization is a key driver in the national effort to coordinate and improve the quality of ADHD care, working closely with the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]] to address systemic challenges in Danish psychiatry [^src1].

### Collaboration and Strategic Alignment
DMPGer maintains a tight collaborative relationship with the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]]. This alignment is structurally reinforced by overlapping membership in their respective steering groups, ensuring that clinical guidelines and database quality indicators are harmonized [^src1]. This partnership is part of a broader political and professional mobilization—alongside the national 10-year plan for psychiatry—aimed at resolving a systemic crisis in ADHD care quality, where several process indicators have historically fallen far below the 90% standard.

### Influence on Quality Indicators and Clinical Practice
The guidelines developed by DMPGer directly underpin and inform the national quality indicators monitored by the ADHD Database. For instance, DMPGer's guidelines are foundational to [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]], which mandates clinical environmental observation in a child's own environment for preschool-aged children to ensure diagnostic certainty regarding ADHD and potential comorbidities [^src4]. Furthermore, an upcoming DMPG guideline focusing on the non-pharmacological treatment of ADHD is expected to provide the necessary evidence to refine and sharpen [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], making it a more meaningful metric for quality improvement [^src2].

The national [[styregruppen|Styregruppen]] (Steering Group) relies heavily on DMPGer's recommendations when making structural decisions about ADHD assessments. Based on DMPG guidelines, the Steering Group has determined that somatic examinations are an essential component of the ADHD diagnostic process [^src3]. 

### Regional Implementation
The clinical authority of DMPGer's guidelines has prompted direct changes in regional healthcare practices. Following recommendations in recent DMPG guidelines regarding ADHD assessment, both [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] and [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] have actively reprioritized their resources to ensure that somatic examinations are consistently performed on patients [^src3].
